chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Azrami, from his father, who said:

When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to solemnize a marriage, he would say: 'All praise is for Allah, I praise Him and seek His help, and I believe in Him and rely upon Him, and I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with Guidance and the Religion of Truth to make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike it. And may Allah bless Muhammad and his Progeny, and peace and mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you.'

'I advise you, servants of Allah, with the fear of Allah, the Guardian of the Bounties and Mercy, Creator of the beings and Manager of their affairs with Power and Mastery. Indeed, to Allah belongs the praise for what is to come and what has passed. To Him belongs exclusive praise and sincere eulogy for whatever grace from Him has been a bountiful blessing to us, a covering upon us, and an adornment for us; the Creator of what is honored and the humbler of what is difficult, the facilitator of what is hard, and the achiever of what is easy.'

'The Initiator of creation with an initial beginning, on the day He originated the sky while it was smoke, so He said to it and the earth: 'Come willingly or unwillingly.' They said: 'We come willingly.' So He completed them as seven heavens in two days. And neither does a severe [force] confuse Him, nor does a fleeing one precede Him, nor does a departing one escape Him. On the Day when every soul is paid what it has earned, and they are not wronged.'
ai.seo_question: What is the traditional supplication recited by Imam Ali (AS) during marriage ceremonies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* preserves the liturgical protocol of Imam Ali (AS) for marriage, blending the *Khutbah al-Shawk* (Sermon of Need) structure with specific marital blessings. It highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating theological affirmation of Tawhid and Nabuwwah with practical social rites, serving as a model for the spiritual sanctification of the marital bond.
